title: Choose the visual world for SmartFlow NLEX (round 2)
question: Steered to modern, advanced and blue, with a 3D corridor and a car you can drag on the Overview. Both mocks use the live counts from 3 Oct 22:56. Pick one, re-roll, or take the category standard.

options.label: Lane Signal
options.lineage: overhead lane-control signals on NLEX gantries at night
options.thesis: State speaks the road's own signal language: a green arrow, an amber diagonal, a red cross over each lane.
options.viewport: A chase-camera 3D corridor: drag the car down the road, gantries over each exit carry NB and SB state, a readout follows the car; a km ruler and three signal counts below.
options.risk: Dark-first; the light theme must be designed separately, and lane-signal glyphs must stay a state vocabulary, never decoration.

raised.raise: Guide words: every corridor view names the first and last exit in sight.
One action colour (sky blue) appears only on what you can press or drag.
One reversed plate per screen, reserved for the worst reading.
Focusing an exit dims the rest of the corridor.
The 5 km grid stays visible as the scene's armature.
Dense tabular km numerals along every ruler and margin.

options.label: Radar Composite
options.lineage: PAGASA radar composites and forecast bulletins
options.thesis: Every reading is issued, valid for a window, and drawn on the real map like a weather product.
materials: Public Sans and Red Hat Mono
options.viewport: A bulletin column (issued, valid, source, age, counts, slowest) beside a 3D plate of the real NLEX geometry; drag the car along the true road shape.
options.risk: Light-first, and the most expected look for a forecasting product; the 3D plate has to earn its space over the Live Map's 2D view.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Barcode columns and sine lattices in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A strobing bar field with dense numbers in the margin.
options.case: Black and white only cannot carry road state, and strobing is wrong for a control room.
options.kept: Dense tabular numerals in the margins.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Guide words name the span you are inside.
options.viewport: Text columns with colour quarantined in plates.
options.case: A reading artifact, not an operating surface; cream is the wrong light.
options.kept: Guide words: first and last exit in view.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards with one action colour.
options.viewport: A single scrolling column of friendly cards.
options.case: Friendly consumer softness undercuts an operations tool.
options.kept: One action colour, only where something can be done.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides of columns on a lit bed.
options.case: Raked containers fight scanning; goldenrod is off the brief's blue.
options.kept: One reversed plate per screen for the worst reading.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows.
options.case: Browsing grammar, not monitoring; hides the corridor's continuity.
options.kept: Focus expands one exit and dims the rest.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Huge grid-built numerals over a visible armature.
options.case: Poster type at that scale crowds out the task.
options.kept: The km grid visible as the armature.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean ops dashboard executed well: neutral grey, white cards, one blue.
canonCard.viewport: Stat cards over a corridor card, the arrangement every ops product ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other dashboards by design.
